correctness.rationale: Ultrahomogeneity makes injective ordered-tuple orbits identical to labeled induced finite structures. Choosing which p labels are products gives C(n,p), and each of the n-p consumers independently chooses one of f_p base structures on those same labeled products, proving the transform. Equality patterns give the Stirling transform. For consumer-product, f_p=p!. The upper bound p(n-p)<=n^2/4 and the p=floor(n/2) Stirling lower bound give the 1/4 logarithmic constant. Fresh integer arithmetic reproduces a_1 through a_8 as 2,4,11,54,567,13928,837321,134985098 and the stated full-tuple profile through arity seven.

value.rationale: The result converts a qualitative Fraisse construction into a reusable exact oligomorphic-profile transform for every finite-profile base class. Its consumer-product specialization supplies explicit quantitative invariants and asymptotics for the source's principal example, a natural comparison tool for homogeneous automorphism groups.

final_claim: If a relational Fraisse class has \(f_p\) labeled structures on a fixed p-set, then the diversification limit has injective ordered-tuple orbit profile \(a_n=\sum_{p=0}^n {n\choose p} f_p^{\,n-p}\); for the consumer-product class \(f_p=p!\), giving the stated exact initial profile, Stirling transform for tuples with repetitions, and leading growth constant \(1/4\) in \(\log a_n/(n^2\log n)\).
limitations: The transform assumes a relational base class with finite labeled counts in each finite arity.
The counting argument is short and could exist as unindexed model-theoretic folklore even though no statement-equivalent source was found.
